content.title: About
content.content: Carrots are a root vegetable from the Apiaceae family, cultivated worldwide. Cooked carrots have a tender texture, a mildly sweet flavor, and a bright orange color due to their high beta‑carotene content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Beta‑carotene in carrots is converted to vitamin A, essential for vision.
Carrots come in many colors: orange, yellow, purple, red, and white.
They are believed to boost immunity thanks to antioxidant compounds.
In the 17th century carrots were mostly purple; the orange variety was developed in the Netherlands.

items.title: Supports vision
items.content: Vitamin A derived from beta‑carotene is crucial for retinal health and night vision.

items.title: Antioxidant protection
items.content: Carotenoids and vitamin C help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune system support
items.content: B‑vitamins and minerals contribute to normal immune function.

items.title: Cardiovascular health
items.content: Potassium and dietary fiber aid in blood pressure regulation and cholesterol balance.

items.title: Digestive health
items.content: Fiber promotes intestinal motility and regular bowel movements.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to carrots.

items.title: Excess beta‑carotene
items.content: Very high intake can cause carotenemia – a temporary yellowing of the skin.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: When buying non‑organic carrots, wash them thoroughly to remove possible chemical residues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked carrots can be served as a side dish, added to salads, soups, purees, or incorporated into casseroles. A drizzle of olive oil, a pinch of salt, and fresh herbs enhance their flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked carrots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer keeping, freeze them in portions.
